A_general.open_code_note: The public bolt-js-slack-mcp-server repository is a sample Slack app/client that connects to Slack’s hosted MCP server; it is not the hosted server implementation. The slackapi/slack-skills-plugin repository is a companion skills collection, not the server implementation.
A_general.mcp_protocol_version: JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP; MCP specification version NOT FOUND
A_general.license: N/A for closed hosted server; sample repository license applies to sample only
other_official_servers: Slack’s separate Slackbot MCP client connects Slackbot to third-party MCP servers; it is a client feature, not another server endpoint. https://slack.com/help/articles/48855576908307-Guide-to-the-Slack-MCP-server
A_general.commit_note: commit hash/date filled in by the research script (latest commit on the default branch)

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No standalone MCP server fee or MCP-specific price is stated in the reviewed docs. Access requires a registered Slack app and user authorization; only Slack Marketplace-published or internal apps are permitted. https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Slack plan pricing varies by plan and region; the official pricing page was collected incompletely and exact amounts could not be verified in the prepared evidence. https://slack.com/pricing
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Slack Web API rate limits apply by tool/action type. The official MCP overview lists tiers including Tier 2 (20+ per minute), Tier 3 (50+ per minute), Tier 4 (100+ per minute), and special limits for message/file search and sending. https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: A registered Slack app with fixed app ID is required; app must be Marketplace-published or internal. Workspace admins can approve and manage MCP client integrations. Configured app IP allowlists also apply. Enterprise+ customers using Okta can manage access through their identity provider; Enterprise-Managed Authorization is documented for Slack Enterprise+ and Claude Team/Enterprise. https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/ https://slack.com/help/articles/54548358406419-Manage-access-to-the-Slack-MCP-server-through-your-identity-provider
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Slack controls eligibility and platform behavior; workspace/org admins control app approval and identity-provider provisioning; app owners configure app identity and any IP allowlist.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Hosted tools search Slack content, read and send/schedule/draft messages, manage conversations, reactions, canvases, users, files and lists. Official documentation describes tool categories and rate limits but does not publish a single complete machine-readable tool schema. The attached actions.json records documented/native tool names and marks parameters unpublished where unavailable.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool results and errors use MCP/JSON-RPC; detailed result schemas and error catalog were not found.

Slack says requests are associated with the registered app for logging, rate limits and access control, and directs customers to audit MCP activity using associated audit logs. https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with JSON-RPC error missing_token and a Bearer challenge pointing to https://mcp.slack.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. That resource metadata identifies https://mcp.slack.com as authorization server; bearer methods header/form; TLS-bound tokens false; and scopes_supported: canvases:read, canvases:write, channels:history, channels:read, channels:write, chat:write, emoji:read, files:read, files:write, groups:history, groups:read, groups:write, im:history, im:read, im:write, lists:read, lists:write, mpim:history, mpim:read, mpim:write, reactions:read, reactions:write, search:read.files, search:read.im, search:read.mpim, search:read.private, search:read.public, search:read.users, users:read, users:read.email. Authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code, refresh_token, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer; token endpoint auth client_secret_post; PKCE S256; authorization endpoint https://slack.com/oauth/v2_user/authorize; token endpoint https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access. Slack docs say no Dynamic Client Registration and require a registered app with fixed app ID and client secret. Metadata does not establish token lifetime or revocation behavior.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthenticated requests return JSON-RPC 2.0 error object; authenticated tool result schemas not published in reviewed docs.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth protected-resource metadata and authorization-server metadata; confidential OAuth with pre-registered Slack app, fixed app ID/client ID and client secret; authorization_code, refresh_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer; client_secret_post; PKCE S256. No DCR per official docs; registration_endpoint absent from metadata. Token lifetime/revocation not found. The resource metadata advertises bearer_methods_supported header and form and the full scopes_supported list above.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tools include read operations and writes such as sending/scheduling messages, creating conversations, reactions, canvases, lists and uploading files. Official docs do not publish readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint or openWorldHint annotations. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or MCP elicitation is documented. Slack describes draft/format/preview messages in AI clients; the file upload flow requires a second completion call before the file becomes visible. 3. OAuth user scopes are listed by tool; docs describe user-authorized actions on the user’s behalf. App approval, Marketplace/internal app eligibility and optional IP allowlisting apply. Workspace admins manage approved integrations; Enterprise+ IdP options are documented. 4. No read-only endpoint, toolsets filter or query-free mode documented; one Streamable HTTP endpoint. SSE unsupported. 5. Search supports content and metadata filters; full profile information includes custom fields/statuses. No MCP-specific masking documented. 6. Per-tool/action Web API rate limits apply; overview lists Tier 2/3/4 and special limits. 7. Parameter validation/correction behavior not documented. 8. Slack says requests are associated with app for logging, rate limits and access control; advises audit via associated audit logs. Telemetry/retention specifics not found. 9. No vendor feedback/rating/reporting tool is named in the documented MCP tool categories; no tool-level upsell found. 10. Slack’s companion skills plugin distributes skills outside MCP. No server-delivered skill tool documented. 11. Cross-session memory/state behavior not documented. 12. Flat documented hosted service; no sub-server hierarchy described. 13. No raw API/SQL/script escape hatch documented.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official overview is https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/ and describes tool categories and operations, but does not expose a single exact-name, schema-complete list or state a numeric total. Names in actions.json are taken from Slack’s official documentation and companion Slack skills references; descriptions are summarized from the official overview. Parameters are NOT PUBLISHED because the official reviewed sources do not provide the MCP schemas. No catalogue-only tools were added. Third-party catalogue pages were reviewed for cross-checking; neither was treated as authoritative for native names or schemas.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public server code or verbatim complete tool definitions/initialize instructions available; not computed.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Slack humans can perform product operations beyond the documented MCP set, including workspace administration, app management and configuration. The official MCP overview limits its described operations to Slack search, messages, conversations, reactions, canvases, user/profile, file and list operations; exact exhaustive UI/API-only differences were not published in the reviewed MCP reference. https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/ https://slack.com/help/articles/48855576908307-Guide-to-the-Slack-MCP-server

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Slack recommends care when connecting multiple MCP servers and says clients give them access to Slack data as context. The upload workflow is documented as a two-step sequence; no evidence shows the server itself enforces the AI-facing recommendation to follow that sequence beyond requiring the file ID for completion.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Slack says workspace admins can approve/manage MCP client integrations and app identity supports logging, rate limits and access control. It advises auditing MCP activity through associated audit logs. Documentation does not specify retention periods, AI training use, or MCP-specific masking.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Slack describes the connection as secure and says the server enables access to Slack data/actions on behalf of the authenticated user. Admin approval and user OAuth consent are described.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth scopes and API rate limits are exposed through metadata/documentation. App approval and IP allowlists are documented controls. Audit logging is promised/documented but implementation details are not independently verifiable from public server code. No public implementation was found to verify other documentation claims.

contradictions: The provided OAuth authorization-server metadata advertises grant_types_supported including refresh_token and jwt-bearer, while Slack’s overview describes confidential OAuth for MCP clients but does not enumerate those grant types. The metadata is the endpoint’s direct published value.
The resource metadata advertises bearer_methods_supported as header and form; the official docs discuss OAuth client token handling but do not describe form bearer-token use.

Official docs describe message drafting/previewing and list operations, but no complete official tool-name/schema listing was found; exact action names and parameters are therefore less directly documented than the capabilities.
observations_for_research: The service uses confidential OAuth with pre-registered app identity rather than Dynamic Client Registration.
Slack delegates access control to user OAuth scopes and app/workspace approval, while applying the same Web API rate limits to MCP actions.
File upload is described as a two-call flow where the file remains invisible until completion.
Slack publishes a companion skills plugin separately from the hosted server.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ including HTML/script extracts and docs/help pages, and local repository copies. No public implementation of the hosted server was found. The official Slack skills-plugin repository and Bolt JS sample are not the deployed server; the latter is a sample app/client. Endpoint /mcp returned HTTP 401 missing_token; root OAuth protected-resource metadata was provided, while the path-suffixed resource metadata returned 404. Pricing page capture was incomplete, so exact current plan prices are omitted. Unofficial npm package @chinchillaenterprises/mcp-slack was noted but excluded as evidence. The 28 action entries in actions.json reflect documented operation categories and names available in official Slack references; official docs do not state an aggregate tool total or publish complete schemas.
